goals: PRIMARY (mechanistic): quantify hillslope-to-stream travel times including lateral flow convergence along topographic flowpaths
PRIMARY (mechanistic): quantify groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
FALLBACK (mechanistic, partial): characterize vertical recharge / sub-surface drainage flux (QDRAI) as a function of topographic position, as the boundary forcing a lateral model would need
key_processes: lateral saturated subsurface flow along hillslope gradient
vertical infiltration and recharge (the only vertically-resolved piece)
drivers_to_resolve: topography (elevation, slope, upslope contributing area / convergence)

model_choice.rationale: The brief is tagged 'site', but the requested physics is lateral and connected, which single-column ELM cannot represent. ELM can only contribute the vertical recharge flux that a lateral model would consume.
model_choice.coupling_note: Answering travel time / lateral convergence would require ELM recharge (QDRAI) to drive a distributed lateral flow + transport model (PFLOTRAN with a hillslope mesh plus particle-tracking/age tracing, and a surface routing scheme for the to-stream leg). ELM->PFLOTRAN coupling is not implemented, and the transport/routing pieces are not framework capabilities. Listed in requires_capabilities.

answerable: Vertical sub-surface drainage / recharge flux (QDRAI) from independent ELM columns, and its qualitative variation with soil texture across topographic positions (soil-driven, NOT elevation-climate-driven under uniform forcing)

not_answerable.why: Single-column 1-D ELM has no lateral routing or transport; there is no mechanism to accumulate residence/travel time along a flowpath. No stream routing capability exists.
not_answerable.needs: distributed lateral flow model + travel-time/particle-tracking transport + surface-to-channel routing

not_answerable.aspect: Lateral flow convergence along topographic flowpaths
not_answerable.why: ELM columns are hydraulically independent; convergence (upslope area concentrating flow into hollows) is a between-column lateral process ELM cannot represent.
not_answerable.needs: distributed/lateral subsurface flow (PFLOTRAN hillslope mesh) driven by upslope-area-aware topography

not_answerable.aspect: Groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
not_answerable.why: No inter-column hydraulic connection in single-column ELM; each column's water table is isolated.
not_answerable.needs: ELM->PFLOTRAN coupling with lateral saturated-zone connectivity

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (topographic-position) — provisional, ONLY meaningful as recharge-BC characterization, not as travel-time resolution
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x 3 topographic-position classes = 9 columns spans the topographic heterogeneity that would set the recharge boundary condition for a downstream lateral model. This N is defensible ONLY for recharge characterization; it does NOT and cannot resolve the requested lateral travel times.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample valley bottoms / riparian corridors and convergent hollows where lateral groundwater exchange and to-stream travel would be strongest — flagged as the priority zones a future lateral model must resolve.
sampling_strategy.replication: none — exploratory scoping only; replication is not justified until a lateral capability exists to consume these fluxes

sampling_plan.reason: Lowest elevation convergent positions where lateral inflow and groundwater-stream exchange concentrate; characterizes near-stream recharge BC (does NOT yield travel time).
Mid-elevation transport zone along flowpaths; provides intermediate recharge flux across hollow/planar/nose positions.
High-elevation flowpath initiation zone; characterizes headwater recharge that a lateral model would route downslope.

validation_design.comparison: none possible — no travel-time observations and no model output to compare
none — brief lists no observations; validation would require analog gauged catchment recharge, clearly labelled as analog if pursued

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline 1980-2018 forcing, native gridded soil per column; NOTE these columns only characterize recharge, not the requested lateral travel times

requires_capabilities.why: to pass vertical recharge into a lateral subsurface flow solver
requires_capabilities.blocks: any lateral flow / groundwater exchange result

requires_capabilities.capability: distributed lateral subsurface flow (PFLOTRAN hillslope mesh with inter-position connectivity)
requires_capabilities.why: to represent flow convergence and neighbor-to-neighbor groundwater exchange

requires_capabilities.capability: subsurface transport / particle-tracking or groundwater-age tracer
requires_capabilities.why: travel time is a transport quantity, not a flux
the 'to-stream' leg of travel time needs overland/channel routing

requires_capabilities.capability: topographic flowpath / upslope-contributing-area extraction from DEM
requires_capabilities.why: convergence and flowpath geometry must be derived from the DEM
under uniform forcing, elevation-stratified columns vary only by soil, so topographic climate control on recharge is not isolated
requires_capabilities.blocks: attributing recharge variation to elevation/climate vs soil

requires_capabilities.why: to assign native soil and topographic class per column

assumptions: Brief lists no observations, so no validation of any target is possible in-domain.
Forcing is spatially uniform across the domain unless downscaling is added; elevation-stratified columns therefore differ by soil, not climate.
The 9-column stratification is scoped ONLY as recharge-BC characterization and is not represented as answering the travel-time question.
PFLOTRAN, though available, is described as steady-state groundwater and lacks the transport/routing needed for travel times as posed.
open_questions: Is the deliverable actual quantitative travel-time distributions, or a qualitative ranking of hillslope positions by recharge? The former is currently infeasible.
Are there any streamflow, water-table, or tracer/age observations in or near the Naches that could anchor a future lateral model?
Would the user accept an analog-catchment or literature-based travel-time framing while the lateral coupling backlog is built?
Is elevation-downscaled forcing available or plannable, given topographic climate control is central to Naches hydrology?
